Hi Ava / Jordan —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: Run a customer-specific evaluation on your triage/suggestion model to confirm latency constraints and quality against your in-house rule set (priority intents + hallucination threshold).
- Success criteria (what you asked for): 1) >= 92% match on intent classification on our pass/fail prompt set, 2) < 1% critical hallucination rate as measured by your eval rubric, 3) p95 latency < 450ms on a dedicated Redwood instance with 1x GPU.

Proposed immediate deliverables:
1) Redwood provides an eval harness and a short reference benchmark (notebook + instructions). See attached "redwood_eval_instructions.pdf".
2) Medexa shares a representative sample dataset (we suggested ~1,200 labeled prompts) in JSONL format and a small holdout validation set. We attached a simple CSV with example prompts (medexa_sample_prompts.csv) to show acceptable fields.
3) We run three model candidates (open-llama-7b-quant, redwood-compat-13b-fp16, and a distilled 7B variant) and return: prompt/response pairs, automatic scoring, and flagged regressions.
4) Technical touchpoint: Marissa (solutions) + Dylan (ML infra) will own the onboarding and run. We propose kickoff tomorrow at 10:00am PT for SFTP/Drive access and schema alignment.

Next steps for you (can you confirm by EOD?):
- Share a redacted JSONL sample (1k-1.5k entries) and the scoring rubric you use for hallucination severity.
- Confirm whether PII will be present (so we can recommend Private deployment or tokenization options).

I left the proposed kickoff calendar hold (tentative). If tomorrow 10:00am PT doesn’t work, suggest two alternatives.

Thanks — looking forward to running the evals.

Best,
Karthik

Hi Ava / Jordan —

Thanks — confirmed for 10:00am PT. Quick technical spec and what the harness will give you so you can prep the JSONL and rubric: 

JSONL spec (single-line JSON per record, UTF-8):
- id (string) — unique id matching your records
- user_text (string) — the prompt/question
- context (array of strings) — optional prior messages (can be empty)
- gold_intent (string) — your human-annotated intent label
- severity_label (string) — one of informational/incorrect/critical
- metadata (object) — keep flat key:value strings, e.g., channel:email

If you prefer CSV, we can ingest that too but JSONL preserves context arrays. Attached is a small example JSONL and a CSV-derived sample (medexa_eval_template.jsonl).

Eval harness output (what Redwood will return):
- Per-prompt model_response, auto-intent (model-predicted label), intent_confidence (0-1), hallucination_flag (binary), hallucination_score (0-1), latency_ms.
- Aggregate reports: precision/recall per intent, confusion matrix, hallucination by severity bucket, and token-level cost.
- Regression detection: we run a baseline against your holdout and flag prompts where model response quality drops > 10 points vs baseline (we'll show diffs and sample responses).

Scoring guidance (short):
- For hallucination detection we combine a simple heuristic (knowledge-cutoff checks + entity hallucination matching against provided context) and your severity labels for calibration.
- If the quality delta stems from instruction sensitivity (few-shotness), we recommend prompt tuning first (few-shot examples + constrained decoding). If the gap is architectural (missing capacity to capture domain nuance), we recommend trying the 13B fp16 variant. We'll provide concrete A/B examples in the first report.

Operational notes: 
- Given PHI, this will be run in a Private project under your VPC. Please confirm network allowlist and KMS details during kickoff.
- Expected run time for 1.2k examples across three model candidates: ~45-60 minutes (including automatic metric generation).

Kickoff agenda (20m):
1) Transfer method & schema validation (5m)
2) Confirm scoring rubric + labeling semantics (5m)
3) Walk through what the harness will output (5m)
4) Next steps & timing for a follow-up results review (5m)

Let me know if you want us to include any additional metrics (we can add BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics but for your use case we'll prioritize intent and hallucination metrics).

See you tomorrow,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
